text: Did you know every hot dog you put in your mouth gets stripped naked first?
Relax. Today I'll show you why.
Crushed ice, a skin that isn't meat, a 155-degree oven… and a secret fourth step.
say: Crushed ice, a skin that isn't meat, a one fifty-five degree oven… and a secret fourth step.

text: A hot dog is a long, tender tube of finely ground meat, made for a bun.
But what happens before it reaches your home?
Step one: meat chopped with crushed ice into a paste.
The fat goes in last, ice cold: if it warms up, the hot dog sweats fat.
Step two: the paste gets pushed under pressure into a cellulose casing.
And here, size does matter: the casing decides how thick it gets.
A machine twists it, and out come the links.
Step three: the oven, to 155 degrees inside, then a cold shower.
say: Step three: the oven, to one fifty-five degrees inside, then a cold shower.

text: Nope. Cellulose doesn't digest. Hence, step four.
Steam, a blade slits it open, and a jet of air rips it off.
Like peeling the plastic off a brand-new phone.
As it cooks, the outer meat sets into its own skin.
Erwin Freund figured that out in the 1920s… by accident.
say: Erwin Froind figured that out in the nineteen twenties… by accident.

text: Before: a paste full of ice. Now: a naked hot dog with your friend's name on it.
